body:
> Found piloting hkb on `french-tech-homies/pipao-v2` on 2026-08-27/28: one goal decomposed into two roots, 11 nodes, 13 PRs. Two gaps in `/kanban:decompose`, both cheap to close in `skills/kanban/SKILL.md`.

## Gap 1 — a sibling root's number is never written back

The materialization order in *"3. Materialize, in this order"* is: root body → children (parents first, so `--blocked-by` numbers exist) → `hkb link` → `promote` → graph comment. That fills in **child** numbers correctly, because `hkb link` supplies them.

It has no step for a **second root** created later. When a goal is too big for one track and gets split into two, the first root's body is written *before* the second root exists, so it can only describe it in prose.

What happened: #103's body said item 3 "was cut into its own root on 2026-08-27" with no number. The worker running #103's synthesize pass was told to move leftover open work onto the board, could not find the sibling, and **recreated the entire Radix-retirement backlog** as a new issue duplicating four already-decomposed children. It was caught in triage, but a promoted duplicate would have burned a full worker session redoing decomposed work.

**Fix:** add a step (f) — after both roots exist, patch each root's body with the other's number. Or advise creating both roots up front, numbers first, bodies second.

## Gap 2 — path-disjoint siblings still conflict at merge

The guidance says *"Disjoint `paths` buy parallelism"* and *"siblings meant to run at once must own different files"*, which is true for the `path_overlap` guard. But the guard prevents **concurrency**, not **divergent bases**: two siblings branched from different points on the default branch will conflict at merge whenever they touch the same file, however well the guard sequenced them.

Three of thirteen PRs needed a hand-merge for exactly this, all in generated or append-only files:

- `registry.json` + `public/r/*.json` — regenerated by every node that adds a component
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md` — every node appends at the same anchor
- `package.json` + `package-lock.json` — one node bumped a version, another added devDependencies; the auto-merge produced a lock disagreeing with the manifest, which fails `npm ci`

One was a **semantic** conflict git could not see: node A spread a `...stamp` into every registry item constructor; node B later added a new constructor; the textual merge kept both and shipped one item unstamped. Node A's own CI guard caught it.

**Fix:** a paragraph in the *"What makes a graph work"* list — when two siblings regenerate the same artifact or append to the same doc, chain them (`--blocked-by`) even though the dependency is not logical. The wall-clock cost is zero whenever the path guard would have serialized them anyway.

## Done when

- [ ] `SKILL.md`'s decompose recipe has a step for writing sibling-root numbers back.
- [ ] *"What makes a graph work"* warns that disjoint paths do not prevent merge conflicts, with the generated-artifact and append-only-doc cases named.
- [ ] `references/protocol.md`'s worked example stays consistent with both.
goal: SKILL.md has a step for writing sibling-root numbers back, and warns that disjoint paths prevent concurrency but not divergent-base merge conflicts.
title: decompose recipe: sibling-root numbers are never written back, and disjoint paths do not prevent merge conflicts
